cases.purpose: dns query returns the same RRsets and rcodes over UDP, DoT and DoH for multi-record A, MX, TXT, NODATA, NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL answers (r4).
cases.oracle: A Python mock serves one fixed zone over UDP, RFC 7858 DoT and RFC 8484 DoH; the expected RRsets and rcodes are the zone data written in the fixture (A 192.0.2.10/11, MX 10 mail.x.test., TXT alpha/beta, NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, NODATA), and each transport must equal both the zone and the UDP result.
cases.comparison: Eighteen candidate dns query runs (six questions x three transports) in a mapped user and mount namespace that bind-mounts the fixture CA over the system bundle for curl and uses a PATH holding only a symlink to the candidate for the documented execlp(bash) transports.
cases.setup_script:
mkdir -p "$HOME/pbin"
ln -s /opt/bashos-parity/candidate "$HOME/pbin/bash"
printf "nameserver 127.0.0.1\n" > resolv.conf
openssl req -x509 -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:prime256v1 -nodes -keyout "$HOME/tls.key" -out "$HOME/tls.crt" -days 2 -subj /CN=127.0.0.1 -addext subjectAltName=IP:127.0.0.1 -addext basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE 2>"$HOME/openssl.log"

files.transport.sh:
export BASHDNS_RESOLV_CONF="$PWD/resolv.conf"
for q in "www.x.test A" "x.test MX" "txt.x.test TXT" "nx.x.test A" "fail.x.test A" "www.x.test TXT"; do
  set -- $q
  BASHDNS_SERVER_PORT=5301 dns query "$1" "$2" -s 127.0.0.1 > "u-$1-$2.out" 2> "u-$1-$2.err"; echo "$?" > "u-$1-$2.rc"
  dns query "$1" "$2" --dot -h 127.0.0.1:5302 --dot-ca "$HOME/tls.crt" > "d-$1-$2.out" 2> "d-$1-$2.err"; echo "$?" > "d-$1-$2.rc"
  dns query "$1" "$2" --doh https://127.0.0.1:5303/dns-query > "h-$1-$2.out" 2> "h-$1-$2.err"; echo "$?" > "h-$1-$2.rc"
done

cases.script:
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/mig-w2-dnsx.py
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" mock 5301 5302 5303 ready 2> mock.err &
srv=$!
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" waitport 5302 5303
/usr/bin/unshare --user --map-root-user --mount "$BASH" --noprofile --norc ./q.sh
echo "transport-run-rc=$?"
kill "$srv"; wait "$srv" 2>/dev/null
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" verify-r4

cases.purpose: auth-serve --tls-listen/--doh-listen serve the same zone to independent Python DoT and DoH (HTTP/1.1 POST and GET) clients, and the DoH TLS handshake succeeds (r5).
cases.oracle: Independent Python ssl/http.client clients with a fixed expectation (www.x.test A = 192.0.2.10 and 192.0.2.11, NOERROR), RFC 7858 framing and RFC 8484 POST/GET; separate probes isolate the TLS handshake (with ALPN offered) from the HTTP request and DNS message handling.
cases.comparison: Candidate auth-serve with a TLS and a DoH listener on loopback; four probes print only failing lines plus a summary that must report failed=0.
cases.setup_script: openssl req -x509 -newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:prime256v1 -nodes -keyout "$HOME/tls.key" -out "$HOME/tls.crt" -days 2 -subj /CN=127.0.0.1 -addext subjectAltName=IP:127.0.0.1 -addext basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE 2>"$HOME/openssl.log"

files.x.zone:
$ORIGIN x.test.
$TTL 300
@ IN SOA ns1.x.test. hostmaster.x.test. 1 3600 600 86400 300
@ IN NS ns1.x.test.
@ IN MX 10 mail.x.test.
ns1 IN A 192.0.2.53
www IN A 192.0.2.10
www IN A 192.0.2.11
mail IN A 192.0.2.25
txt IN TXT "alpha"
txt IN TXT "beta"

cases.script:
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/mig-w2-dnsx.py
dns auth-serve --zone x.zone --listen 127.0.0.1 --port 5311 --tls-listen 127.0.0.1:5312 --tls-cert "$HOME/tls.crt" --tls-key "$HOME/tls.key" --doh-listen 127.0.0.1:5313 --doh-cert "$HOME/tls.crt" --doh-key "$HOME/tls.key" < /dev/null 2> serve.err &
srv=$!
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" waitport 5312 5313
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" probe 5312 5313
kill "$srv"; wait "$srv" 2>/dev/null
true
